old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a grill where various pieces of meat and vegetables are being cooked. The focus is on the sizzling and browning process of the food items. Initially, the camera captures a series of grilled pork belly slices, their surfaces marked with distinct grill lines and a golden-brown hue, indicating they are well-cooked. The view remains static, revealing kimchi, a traditional Korean dish made from fermented cabbage and radish, generously coated with a vibrant red chili paste. The kimchi appears to be slightly softening and releasing its juices, which glisten under the light. The background remains blurred, emphasizing the food and the cooking process. The overall scene suggests a delicious meal being prepared, likely in a Korean restaurant or a home kitchen setting.

caption: The video showcases a close-up view of food sizzling on a flat, dark, oily griddle. Neat rows of sliced pork belly fill the center and right, their edges browned and their surfaces glistening with rendered fat that catches shifting specular highlights. On the left sits a heap of red chili-coated cabbage, its pale stems and thin white enoki-like strands matted with sauce. Thin wisps of steam drift continuously above the meat, changing shape and position from moment to moment. Small bubbles form and pop in the fat, marking an ongoing sizzle rather than any new action. No tools touch the food, and the pieces themselves remain fixed in place throughout the excerpt. A slow, slight camera drift gradually reveals more of the left kimchi pile and the dark upper rim of the grill, nudging the meat rows toward the right edge. The cooking simply continues, unhurried, across every frame.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
